newsitem.title: FRANCE: France concerned on Israeli building in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: France concerned on Israeli building in Jerusalem.

text.p: France is concerned about Israeli plans to build new housing for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem, the French foreign ministry said on Friday.

"French authorities fear the building of new projects will put an end to the climate of confidence which had again surfaced after the agreement on Hebron," foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pledged on Wednesday to build 6,500 Jewish homes at Jabal Abu Ghneim or Har Homa, a hill of pine trees between Jerusalem and Bethlehem captured by Israel in the 1967 war.

Critics say the plan would spark Palestinian rage that could prove more costly than gun battles in which 61 Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers died last year after Netanyahu opened a new entrance to a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.

"French authorities reaffirm their attachment to the Israel-Palestinian accords which stipulated the maintaining of a status quo in Jerusalem as long as a new accord on a final status was not reached," Rummelhardt said.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Thursday urged international backers of the Middle East peace process to force Israel to abide by the accords.
Rummelhardt said Arafat, who was expected in Brussels on Monday, would visit Paris for talks shortly afterwards.
French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette will in turn visit Israel, Lebanon and Syria from March 4-6, he said.
Much of that visit will be devoted to seeking ways of calming the situation on the Israel-Lebanon border and seeking a solution involving all the countries in the area.
The subject was discussed in Damascus on Thursday when Syrian President Hafez al-Assad received a senior French diplomat who conveyed a message about the peace process from President Jacques Chirac.
